findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain food debris or chipping/ pitting:
1) 2 knives were stored in a ready to use position with food debris on them. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the knives to be cleaned and sanitized.
2) One spatula was chipped and contained pitting. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the item.
Ensure food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch, to prevent contaminating ready to eat (RTE) foods items. Equipment that contains pitting or breakage could potentially contaminate RTE foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 2 bottles of milk in the Newborn room mini-fridge to be above recommended cold holding temperatures. Milk was probed at 48F.  Classroom teacher stated that the milk was brought in by the parent one hour prior to the temperature being taken. CORRECTED- Milk was moved into working refrigerator in the cafeteria. Ensure all TCS foods are held in units that are being cold held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the cold holding unit in the Newborn room to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Inspector will return on 10/07/25 to ensure that the cold holding unit has been repaired or replaced. Do not store TCS items in this mini-fridge until the food items can hold an internal temperature of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the cold holding units in the newborn and toddler rooms to not have ambient thermometers. CORRECTED- the PIC placed ambient thermometers in the front of the cold holding units. Ensure all cold holding units that contain TCS foods have an ambient thermometer in the warmest region to monitor the temperature of the unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 doors to have a sizable gap in the bottom left corner. These doors are located at the kitchen loading zone, the cafeteria, and south hallway door between the classrooms and the cafeteria. These openings could allow for the entry of pests. Extend or replace door sweeps by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 2 different Food Handlers Certificates to be expired. Ensure Food Handlers Certificates are acquired within 30 days of hire, and renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The PIC present during breakfast service (at the beginning of the inspection) does not have a current food handler certificate. CORRECTED- A CFM arrived shortly after the beginning of the inspection. Ensure a CFM is present during all times of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment: Restrooms in hallway between classrooms and front office were observed with broken self-closers. Owner noted the doors are hollow and require special plates to be installed on the backside of the door that will allow for re-attachment of and proper function of the self-closers.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 A toilet room located on the premises shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight- fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Open can of soda was observed on shelving used for clean dish storage. Employee helping in kitchen noted it was their personal beverage. Soda was relocated to the counter by the service window away from clean dish storage and food prep area. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14 Restrooms in hallway between classrooms and front office were observed with broken self-closers. Owner noted the doors are hollow and require special plates to be installed on the backside of the door that will allow for re-attachment of and proper function of the self-closers. 
A toilet room located on the premises shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight- fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreements were not on file for the main cook and the employee assisting with food prep today. Employee health policy was discussed, and reporting agreements were signed by the staff working in the kitchen today as well as the owners since they too sometimes assist with food prep. Owner noted at the next meeting all current staff would be asked to sign a reporting agreement and moving forward it will be included in the new hire packet for employees to sign. That way, if any staff need to assist in the kitchen they have the reporting agreements on file. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket was observed at 0ppm quat in the kitchen, and the sanitizer solution at the 3 part sink was at a concentration below 200ppm. Quat product used has a listed effective concentration of 200-400ppm on the label directions. Solutions in question were prepared around 6:30am and were in need of changing. Fresh solutions were prepared and observed at 200-400ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration, and change solutions as needed throughout daily operations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Gaps were observed in the juncture between the mopsink and the wall. Seal the mopsink to the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
